summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of NSTEMI and ventricular tachycardia was admitted after an asymptomatic episode of sustained monomorphic VT during dialysis. She was treated with IV amiodarone and magnesium, converted to sinus rhythm, and started on oral amiodarone and mexiletine with close QTc monitoring. Her QTc peaked at 530 ms but improved to 460 ms by discharge. She had melena on admission due to bleeding gastric polyps, with hemoglobin declining from 10.3 to 7.8 g/dL, but it stabilized without transfusion. Pain from calciphylaxis was managed with increased fentanyl patch and Dilaudid; IV thiosulfate was deferred due to arrhythmia risk. She received dialysis and a fistulogram during admission, was evaluated by dermatology, wound care, and palliative care, and was discharged to extended care with plans for wound management, medication adherence, and follow-up.
